items.summary_original: the house learned how to hide movement Most houses have a room whose only purpose is to get you somewhere else. Most of us are so used to the idea of the hallway that it's hard to imagine it was ever novel. Yet for much of architectural history, especially in large European villas, movement worked differently. Rooms were organized as a cluster so that they each opened directly into each other. items.title: superstudio’s 12 ideal cities question the price of a perfectly designed life
items.summary_original: Superstudio designed 12 impossible ways of living In 1971, Superstudio imagined twelve cities designed to solve the problems of human existence and came up with solutions so complete that there was barely any life left to live. A person wakes up in a five-cubit cell. The temperature is permanently set at 25°C. The humidity never changes. Food and every other necessity arrive automatically. There is no work to do, no reason to leave, and no one else to meet. The room knows what its inhabitant wants before they have to ask. It also knows when they are unhappy. items.summary_original: Raw Metal and Pale Blue Accents Give Mellow Cafe Its Identity Mellow Cafe is an unbuilt interior concept for a compact takeaway coffee shop in Mulhouse, France . Developed by Wrong Door Studio, the project explores how a small commercial footprint can become a distinctive hospitality experience through a clear spatial strategy, expressive materials, and carefully integrated functional elements. The concept is built around efficiency and intuitive customer flow. Rather than filling the limited space with decorative elements, the design uses the architecture itself to organize the experience, from ordering and preparation to pick-up and product display. Das von Wrong Door Studio entwickelte Projekt untersucht, wie eine kleine kommerzielle Fläche durch eine klare räumliche Strategie, ausdrucksstarke Materialien und sorgfältig integrierte Funktionselemente zu einem unverwechselbaren Gastfreundschaftserlebnis werden kann. Das Konzept basiert auf Effizienz und intuitivem Kundenfluss. Anstatt den begrenzten Raum mit dekorativen Elementen zu füllen, nutzt das Design die Architektur selbst, um das Erlebnis zu organisieren, von der Bestellung und Vorbereitung bis zur Abholung und Produktpräsentation. items.summary_original: Weirdo helped the British fashion brand swap the usual models for "open-minded" women aged 19 to 72, found via guerrilla posters, shot in a single day and backed by new positioning and a signature colour called Lemonade. I have fond memories of Topshop and Tammy Girl in my teens, and of watching The Clothes Show every Sunday evening with my mam, while my dad disappeared upstairs to tinker on the computer. Brands like Whistles came much later. It was always considered pricey and high-end compared to other high street stores, so we never shopped there. As soon as I started earning my own money, though, I saved every penny to get the latest cuts. I remember one pair of black trousers that I treated like a precious treasure f

items.summary_original: The independent studio reframes "psychic guidance" for modern life, with stunning illustrations by María Jesús Contreras. When I saw the name Keen land in my inbox on Wednesday night, I immediately thought of the dorky-turned-cool footwear brand I love so much. Alas, it wasn't. Instead of walking shoes and unconventional sandals, this Keen is known as a leading online marketplace that connects people with spiritual advisors. Good lord. There must be a lot of money in psychic services because they've just had a rebrand courtesy of Mother Design, part of the Mother family. items.title: Building A UX ROI Case That Survives The Boardroom
items.summary_original: Sooner or later, a CFO looks at your wireframes and asks what any of it actually does for the bottom line. Storyboards don’t answer that question, and the era when a 5-minute pitch could answer it ended, unfortunately, a while ago. These days, if you want to win budget, buy-in, and backing for UX , the design has to be provably good for the business, not only for the people using it. And proving that takes more than taping a dollar sign to a redesign. You have to understand how your organization defines value in the first place, how it measures that value, and how a credible line gets drawn between a design initiative and an outcome leadership already cares about. Designed by Vladislav Gaiduk, founder of the multidisciplinary architecture studio, the 338-sqm interior responds to a brief for a flexible gallery that meets international curatorial standards and accommodates work ranging from paintings to installations . The layout began with an L-shaped unit. MAST reorganized it around a clear rectangular volume, placing an office area at the center and an exhibition hall on either side. A separate portion contains the museum room and storage. Keeping partitions to a minimum gives large works room to be viewed

items.title: What Shakespeare got right about AI
items.summary_original: From ink and quill to glowing code: Shakespeare’s exploration of prophecy and equivocation, the art of speaking truths that mislead, anticipates the central challenge of our own relationship with artificial intelligence. Every warning we need about AI was written four hundred years ago. What witches, a forged letter, and a haunted prince can teach you about talking to a machine. The sharpest words ever written about artificial intelligence came from a man who never had electricity, a telephone, or a single line of code. He’s been dead four hundred years, and he still wrote thirty-seven plays about it. The obvious place to look for AI is science fiction, and plenty of people have gone looking. items.title_de: Was Shakespeare über KI richtig gemacht hat
items.summary_de: Von Tinte und Feder zum leuchtenden Code: Shakespeares Erforschung von Prophezeiung und Zweideutigkeit, der Kunst, irreführende Wahrheiten auszusprechen, nimmt die zentrale Herausforderung unserer eigenen Beziehung zur künstlichen Intelligenz vorweg. Jede Warnung, die wir über KI brauchen, wurde vor vierhundert Jahren geschrieben. Was Ihnen Hexen, ein gefälschter Brief und ein heimgesuchter Prinz über das Sprechen mit einer Maschine beibringen können. Die schärfsten Worte, die jemals über künstliche Intelligenz geschrieben wurden, kamen von einem Mann, der nie Strom, ein Telefon oder eine einzige Codezeile hatte. Er ist seit vierhundert Jahren tot und hat immer noch siebenunddreißig Stücke darüber geschrieben. Der offensichtliche Ort, an dem man nach KI suchen sollte, ist Science-Fiction, und viele Leute haben sich auf die Suche gemacht. Patrick Neeman hat einen guten Teil dieses Jahres damit verbracht, Star Wars, Matrix und Minority R zu benoten

items.title: IED master of arts graduates deploy design against the loss of common goods
items.summary_original: IED MASTERS of arts EVOLVE PRACTICE THROUGH DESIGN X COMMONS Marking an evolution in how design intervenes within contemporary society, the Master of Arts programs at Istituto Europeo di Design (IED) treat the discipline as a mediator between communities and common goods. Grounded in the understanding of commons as the material and immaterial resources that multiple communities engage with as the collective heritage of humanity, the overarching theme of Design X Commons elevates these graduate thesis projects past formal styling exercises and traditional product development. Combining research alongside speculative design strategies, the emerging designers confront climate vulnerability, urban privatization, labor exploitation, and spatial inequality to reshape collective urban futures. items.summary_original: rodolphe parente and marion mailaender reimagine ken club Rodolphe Parente and Marion Mailaender reimagine Paris’ Ken Club as an architecture in motion, bringing the 1985 identity of the fitness and social club into a contemporary setting opposite the Eiffel Tower . The architects approach the past as an architectural remix, shaping a place where the visual language and atmosphere of the 1980s are sampled, reworked, and given a new rhythm. Parente and Mailaender imagine the club almost as a film set built to last, recreating the atmosphere of another era without turning the interiors into a period replica.
